executionStacks.finding: The production Graph path calls runExecutionOrchestrator WITHOUT the DurableRun journal/checkpoint/resume layer. grep of src/runtime/colima-graph-runner.mjs for writeFileSync/checkpoint/journal/appendEvent/persist: 0 matches. All graph node state (executorResults, nodeResults, worktrees maps) is in-memory and lost on process crash.

execution-orchestrator -> runLifecycle bounded repair; but attempt state is in-memory across the graph run
maxRepairAttempts frozen in configuration fingerprint + restored from resume_policy on resume (repair budget survives restart, invariant D4)
repair attempts tracked in-memory in lifecycle transitions
phase_states + completed_phase_ids + newlySkipped preserved; initialState fed to runDecompositionGraph on resume (ready set rebuilt from durable truth, invariant D5)

EXECUTOR_TIMEOUT -> HOLD journaled; timeoutMs frozen in configuration fingerprint

resume from safe boundary; completed phases preserved; read-only requeue
full graph re-run

summary: AutoLoop already possesses a mature, tested durable-execution layer (STACK_A: journal + atomic checkpoint + fingerprint chain + safe resume + manifest; 41 tests green incl. kill/abort/tamper/recovery cases). The production Graph runner (STACK_B) does NOT use it: it invokes runExecutionOrchestrator directly with zero persistence during the run. The dominant gap for the card is therefore NOT 'no durable engine exists' but 'the existing durable engine is not wired into the production Graph path', plus a small set of unproven invariants (telemetry replay-awareness D7 at the durable layer; worktree restoration on resume).
